title: SMARTerV4 (0.5x) Amplification for single-cell or single-nuclei RNASeq Protocol
author: Allen Institute

steps_raw.instruction: SMARTerV4 (0.5x) Amplification for single-cell or single-nuclei RNASeq
Scope and Applicability: Generate full-length cDNA from single cells, or nuclei, using Takara SMARTer V4.
First Strand DNA Synthesis and cDNA Amplification

Warning: Personal Protective Equipment () should be used at all times while operating this protocol. If you are unsure what you should be using, see your immediate supervisor.
Amplified full-length cDNA transcripts from single-cells for purification and validation in downstream applications.
SeraMag Bead Purification using Agilent Bravo Liquid Handling Robot
HT_043 How to Clean Hoods
NOTE: Always use NEW Strip-tube caps when placing caps on tubes - for ALL steps.
Fill a Pre-Amp ice pan with wet ice.
On top of the ice, place a GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block for the samples, another one for reagent aliquoting, and a GeneMate minifuge tube block. Allow to cool for 5 minutes.
Retrieve sample strips from -80 ºC using associated paperwork as a guide, and place these strips, in order, on the pre-cooled GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block in the wet ice pan.

For PatchSeq reactions, use two aluminum cooler blocks and place the 3D printed tube holders on each block prior to retrieving samples. When placing the 0.2 mL sample tubes on the cooler blocks, leave an empty column between each column of samples to allow space for opening the tubes’ flat caps.
Place another GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block at room temperature inside the hood.
Check out the SMART-Seq v4 Ultra Low Input RNA Kit for Sequencing (Takara 634898) along with the associated SeqAmp DNA Polymerase (Takara 638509) kit.
Record the kit ID #s in the upper-left box of the coversheet on the AMP paperwork.
Check out the appropriate SMART-Seq kit for PatchSeq or FACS samples assigned.
Record the kit ID #s in the upper-left box of the coversheet on the AMP paperwork.
Retrieve the SMART-Seq Kit from -20 ºC.
Remove the following kit components and allow to thaw at room temperature:
SMART-Seq sc TSO (ST2196) or SMART-Seq v4 Oligonucleotide (48 μM) (ST0944)
3' SMART-Seq CDS Primer II A (12 µM) ST2197) or 3’ SMART-Seq CDS Primer II A (12 μM) (ST0947)
SMART-Seq sc First Strand Buffer (5X) (ST2199) or 5X Ultra Low First-Strand Buffer (ST0946)
Nuclease-Free Water (ST2187)
10X Lysis Buffer (ST0948)
Elution Buffer (10 mM Tris-Cl, pH 8.5) (ST2204 or ST0770)
Place the following components directly on the pre-chilled GeneMate minifuge tube block on ice:
SMARTScribe™ Reverse Transcriptase (100 U/μL) (ST2198) or (ST0655)
RNase Inhibitor (40 U/μL) (ST2195) or (ST0764)
Take the PCR Primer II A (ST2200) or (ST0945) and place in a blue cooling block in the working 4 ºC.

10X Lysis Buffer (ST0948) and Elution Buffer (ST2204 or ST0770) are not utilized in this SOP, but will be needed for bead cleanup. These reagents may be brought over to the bead cleanup area at this time.
Methodology/Procedures:
First Strand DNA Synthesis:
Spin down the sample strips, two at a time, in the Pre-Amp minifuge for 10 seconds then immediately return them to the GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block in the wet ice pan.
For PatchSeq reactions, transfer the samples with the 3D printed tube holders to a GeneMate 96-well PCR storage rack and spin down at 1000 x g using a PRE-AMP swing-bucket plate centrifuge.
With a witness, verify the strip IDs by reading them out loud while the witness confirms the IDs against the paperwork.
Ensure all strips are orientated correctly with the strip ID number in the ‘A’ position, the buffer type and creation date in the ‘G’ position and the FACS date in the ‘H’ position.

Write the column number on the neck of the H-well tube for easy identification later in the process. If processing more than 1 plate of strips (1 plate or set =12 strips), use a different color marker for labeling the next plate to distinguish different sets of strips.

For PatchSeq reactions, label the cap of each 0.2 mL sample tube with the well position as indicated on the paperwork. If the controls are not in a flat capped strip, transfer the controls to a reagent 8-strip (0.2 mL PCR 8-tube Flex-Free Strip, Attached Clear Flat Caps, Natural USA Scientific 1402-4700) and label the strip to match the original container.
Once thawed, place the following reagents on ice:
SMART-Seq sc TSO (ST2196) or SMART-Seq v4 Oligonucleotide (48 μM) (ST0944)
3' SMART-Seq CDS Primer II A (12 µM) (ST2197) or (ST0947)

Vortex SMART-Seq sc First Strand Buffer (5x) (ST2199) or 5X Ultra Low First-Strand Buffer (ST0946) and place back on room temperature block without spinning down to allow precipitate to dissolve in solution.
On the thermocycler, select folder “S4 Half vol” to access all 0.5X protocols. Start the “72C_6uL” protocol on the thermocycler (72 °C with 105 °C lid, held indefinitely).
Gently pulse vortex (Setting 9 for 10s) the 3’ SMART-Seq CDS Primer II A on the Pre-Amp hood vortex genie.
Spin down the 3’ SMART-Seq CDS Primer II A (ST0947) in the Pre-Amp minifuge to collect it.
Dilute CDS primer from 12 µM to 6 µM: Add 220 µL NFdH20 (water from kit) to the 3'SMART-Seq CDS Primer II A (12 µM) tube (stock at 220 µL).

Write 'D' and 4-digit kit number on 6uM diluted CDS cap, and mark a black stripe on the tube. This indicates that it is now at 6uM. This tube will supply 4 x 96 reactions. Cap, vortex to mix, spin down.
Place a reagent 8-strip (0.2 mL PCR 8-tube Flex-Free Strip, Attached Clear Flat Caps, Natural USA Scientific 1402-4700) in the reagent GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block.

Using the “μL / 8-well strip” calculation on the AMP paperwork (Table 1: CDS Primer Addition), aliquot 16 μL 6 µM 3’SMART-Seq CDS Primer II A (ST0947) into each well of the reagent 8-strip using a P20 @ 16 μL.
Close the caps on this strip and briefly spin down in the Pre-Amp minifuge to collect the volume. Return the reagent strip to its aluminum block on ice.
Cap the diluted CDS primer tube containing the unused portion. Store this in a box for diluted primers at -20 ºC. Unused and undiluted CDS go in a separate labeled box at -20 ºC.

Begin removing caps from the sample tubes by moving the tubes, one at a time, to the room temperature GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block. This is done to limit any aerosol contamination since open tubes are nowhere near the tubes being de-capped.
Remove the caps from the sample strip then return it to the GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block in the ice pan. Repeat until all tubes are de-capped.
For PatchSeq reactions, open the 0.2 mL tubes one at a time by hand or column by column using the 3D-printed tube opener.
Using an 8-channel P10 @ 1μL, add 1μL of 6 µM 3’SMART-Seq CDS Primer II A from the reagent 8-strip into each well of the sample strips.
Take care not to touch the sample with the pipette tips, or to rinse the tips after dispensing.
Visually confirm the addition by checking each pipette tip, and later, checking the sides of the wells during tube capping.
Cap each sample strip as it is transferred, one at a time, to the room temperature block. Using the strip cap tool, seal the sample strip by pushing down onto the strip caps.
Vortex the strips on setting 9 for 10 seconds using the Pre-Amp hood vortex then spin down using the Pre-AMP hood minifuge.
Label the caps to aid in maintaining strip order.
For PatchSeq reactions, close the tubes by hand then use the flat side of the strip cap tool to seal by pushing down onto the tube caps.
Leaving the samples in the 3D printed tube holders and vortex the samples with a GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block on top to prevent the samples dislodging from the 3D printed tube holder.
Return the samples to the GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block in the ice pan.
Bring the samples and a timer, set to 3 minutes, over to the thermocycler running the "72C_6ul" protocol.
Place the samples onto the block, and start the timer as soon as the samples are loaded.
Close and tighten the lid for the remainder of the 3-minute incubation.
Immediately upon completion of the 3-minute incubation, remove samples from the thermocycler and place them back on the GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block in the ice pan.
End the "72C_6ul" protocol on the thermocycler.
Dispose of the reagent 8-strip with 6 µM 3’SMART-Seq CDS Primer II A.
Start the "10ul_RT" protocol (42 °C hold, 42 °C for 90 – 70 °C for 10 minutes – 4 °C indefinitely) on the thermocycler to pre-heat the lid and bring the block up to 42 ºC.
Using the Pre-Amp vortex and minifuge, vortex all the reagents (Table 2: RT Master Mix Preparation) on setting 9 for 10 sec then spin down to collect the volume.
5x Ultra Low First-Strand Buffer contains DTT, which is difficult to get into solution. Check the tube after spinning it down to make sure all the white precipitate is completely dissolved.
Repeat vortexing as needed until the solution is free from any precipitate.
On ice, prepare the RT Master Mix in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf LoBind tube (VWR 80077-230) by adding the black-text colored reagents in the order and volume listed on the right of Table 2.
Add 210 μL of 5x Ultra Low First Strand Buffer using a P1000 @ 210 μL.
Add 52.5 μL of SMART-Seq sc TSO (ST2196) or SMART-Seq V4 Oligonucleotide (48 µM) (ST0944) using a P200 using a P200 @ 52.5 μL.
Add 26.25 μL of RNase Inhibitor (40 U/μL) (ST2195 or ST0764) using a P200 @ 26.25 μL.
Do not add the SMART Scribe Reverse Transcriptase (100 U/μL) (ST0655) at this point.
Using the Pre-Amp vortex and minifuge, vortex the RT Master Mix tube on setting 9 for 5 seconds and then spin it down to collect the volume.
Begin removing caps from the sample tubes by moving the tubes, one at a time, to the room temperature GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block.

Remove the caps from the sample strip then return it to the GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block in the ice pan. This is done to limit any aerosol contamination since open tubes are nowhere near the tubes being de-capped.
Repeat until all tubes are de-capped.
For PatchSeq reactions, open the 0.2 mL tubes one at a time by hand or column by column using the 3D-printed tube opener.
Add the 105 μL of SMARTScribe Reverse Transcriptase (100 U/μL) to the RT Master Mix tube using a P200 @ 105 μL.
Using the Pre-Amp vortex and minifuge, vortex the RT Master Mix tube on setting 9 for 10 seconds and then spin it down to collect the volume.

Aliquot 46.875 μL of the RT Master Mix into a reagent 8-strip (USA Scientific 1402-4700) using a P200 @ 46.875 μL and following the volume instructions listed in the “μl / 8-well strip” box on Table 2.
Add 3.8 μL of RT Master Mix to the sample strips using an 8-channel P10 @ 3.8 μL, taking care not to touch the pipette tips to the sample.
Cap each sample strip by transferring them, one at a time, to the room temperature block. Using the strip cap tool, seal the sample strip by pushing down onto the strip caps.
Vortex the strips on setting 9 for 10 seconds using the Pre-Amp hood vortex then spin down using the Pre-AMP hood minifuge.
Label the caps to aid in maintaining strip order.
For PatchSeq reactions, close the tubes by hand then use the flat side of the strip cap tool to seal by pushing down onto the tube caps.
Leave the samples in the 3D printed tube holders and vortex the samples with a GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block on top to prevent the samples dislodging from the 3D printed tube holder.
Transfer the samples with the 3D printed tube holders to a GeneMate 96-well PCR storage rack and spin down at 1000 x g using a PRE-AMP swing-bucket plate centrifuge.
Return the samples to the GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block in the ice pan.
Bring the samples over to the thermocycler running the “10ul RT” protocol and load them onto the thermocycler block.
Once all samples are loaded and the lid is closed and tightened, advance the thermocycler to begin the RT protocol.
Make sure the protocol has successfully advanced before leaving the instrument.
cDNA Amplification by LD PCR using SeqAmp DNA Polymerase
Approximately 20 minutes before the RT protocol is complete, retrieve the following from the -20 °C working freezer:
SeqAMP DNA Polymerase (ST2192 or ST0784)
SeqAmp CB PCR Buffer (2x) (4 x 5 mL) (ST2193) or 2X SeqAmp PCR Buffer (4 x 1.25 mL) (ST0665)
Take the PCR Primer II A (12 μM) (ST2200 or ST0945) placed in the working 4 °C refrigerator earlier, and place it in the ice pan.
Using the Pre-Amp vortex and minifuge, vortex all the reagents on setting 9 for 10 seconds then spin down to collect the volume.
Place all reagents on ice after being spun down.
On ice, prepare the PCR Master Mix in a 2 mL Eppendorf LoBind tube by adding the reagents in the volume and order listed in Table 3: PCR Master Mix Preparation.
Add 159 μL of nuclease-free water (ST0804) using a P1000 @ 159 μL.
Add 1325 μL of SeqAmp CB PCR Buffer (ST2193) or SeqAmp PCR Buffer (ST0665) by using a P1000 @ 1000 μL and a P1000 @ 325 μL.
Add 53 μL of PCR Primer II A (12 µM) (ST2200 or ST0945) by using a P200 @ 53 μL.
Vortex the 2 mL Eppendorf LoBind tube for 10 seconds on setting 9, and briefly spin down in a Pre-Amp minifuge to collect the volume.
Add 53 μL of SeqAMP DNA Polymerase (ST2192 or ST0784) to the master mix using a P200 @ 53 μL.
Vortex the 2 mL Eppendorf LoBind tube for 10 seconds on setting 9, and briefly spin down in a Pre-Amp minifuge to collect the volume.
Aliquot out the master mix into a new reagent 8 strip (USA Scientific 1402-4700) using a P200 @ 190 μL. Close the caps and spin the strip in a minifuge. This volume is sufficient for all 12 strips.
Begin removing caps from the sample tubes by moving the tubes, one at a time, over to the room temperature GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block.

Remove the caps from the sample strip and then return it to the GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block in the ice pan. This is done to limit any aerosol contamination since open tubes are nowhere near the tubes being de-capped
Repeat until all tubes are de-capped.
For PatchSeq reactions, open the 0.2 mL tubes one at a time by hand or column by column using the 3D-printed tube opener.
Using an 8-channel P20 @ 15 μL, add 15 μL of PCR master mix to each of the sample strips, taking care to not touch the pipette tips to the sample. Use fresh tips when adding master mix to each strip.
Cap each sample strip by transferring them, one at a time, to the room temperature block. Using the strip cap tool, seal the sample strip by pushing down onto the strip caps.
Vortex the strips on setting 9 for 10 seconds and then spin them down using the Pre-Amp hood vortex and minifuge.
Label the caps to aid in maintaining strip order.
For PatchSeq reactions, close the tubes by hand then use the flat side of the strip cap tool to seal by pushing down onto the tube caps.
Leave the samples in the 3D printed tube holders and vortex the samples with a GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block on top to prevent the samples dislodging from the 3D printed tube holder.
Transfer the samples with the 3D printed tube holders to a GeneMate 96-well PCR storage rack and spin down at 1000 x g using a PRE-AMP swing-bucket plate centrifuge.
Return the samples to the GeneMate 96-well aluminum cooler block in the ice pan.

Load the sample strips onto a thermocycler and run the following protocol (Table 4: PCR Program), using the coversheet of the associated amplification paperwork to inform cycling conditions. Make sure to select “S4 Half vol” folder in thermocycler to access all 0.5X PCR programs.
After PCR is complete, remove the strips and end the thermocycler protocol.
Process strips through the SPRI bead cleanup immediately, or store at 4 °C for up to 24 hours.
Follow bead purification on Agilent Bravo robot instructions
Dispose of all used tips and tubes.

Since this is a 0.5X SMARTerV4 protocol, only half the amount of reagents are used for every 96 samples processed. Leftovers from reagents such as diluted CDS primer, 5X SeqAMP buffer, SeqAMP DNA polymerase should be saved and stored in labeled boxes at -20 ºC. These will be used for another 0.5X SMARTer reaction of 96 samples.
Clean the ice pan with RNase Away followed by a 70% EtOH cleaning.
Make sure ice pan is dry before storage.
Follow the HowTo document (HT_043) detailing daily RSeq hood cleaning
Sign the associated amplification paperwork and file in its designated lab area.
Amplified cDNA SeraMag Bead Cleaning Setup
Ensure that SeraMag beads (GE Healthcare 29343057) have equilibrated to room temperature for at least 30 minutes before using them for sample cleanup.

Vortex SeraMag beads until evenly mixed. Referring to Table 5: Cleanup Reagents (found in the paperwork), pipette the required bead volume into a 25 mL divided reagent trough (VWR 41428-958) using the long side of the reservoir.

Add 25.0 µL of SeraMag Beads (0.9x volume) to each well of a 1 mL deep-well Nunc plate (VWR 73520-120) using the 8-channel E4-XLS+ pipette and multi-dispense settings of: 25 µL volume, 6 dispenses, aspiration and dispense speeds of 2.
Seal the bead plate and briefly spin down (1000 x g for 15s), using the PRE-AMP swing-bucket plate centrifuge.
Label the bead plate with a matching ID to the associated amplification plate.
Pour 2 bottles (at least 6 mL total) of Elution Buffer (ST2204 or ST0770) into a new 25 mL divided reagent trough, using the long side.

Using an 8-channel P200 at 120 µL, dispense 120 µL of Elution Buffer into each well of a new 1.2 mL Square-well storage plate (Thermo Scientific AB1127). This will supply Elution Buffer for up to 5 plates.
Seal the elution reagent plate, label it as containing Amplification EB, and briefly spin down (1000 x g for 15s) using PRE-AMP swing-bucket plate centrifuge.
Label a Twin-Tec 96-well PCR plate with the pre-printed label associated with the correct cleaned and eluted amplification ID.
Consult Table 5 (found in the paperwork) for the volume of 80% Ethanol to prepare.
Prepare this in a Pre-AMP hood, using the graduated cylinder adding 100% ABS grade Ethanol (AAPER E200G-P) to a new 500 mL reagent bottle (VWR 28199-760).
Volume should reflect what is listed next to the EtOH box on the paperwork (34.4 mL / plate).
Use a serological pipette to add the listed volume of NFdH2O to the 500 mL reagent bottle (VWR 28199-760) containing the 100% Ethanol to make the final solution 80% (8.6 mL / plate).
Label this 500 mL reagent bottle (VWR 28199-760) “80% EtOH”
Ensure 10X Lysis Buffer (SMART-Seq4 kit: Clontech 634892) has thawed and equilibrated to room temperature.
Pour into a 25 mL divided reservoir (VWR 41428-958) using the long side.

Aliquot 50 µL 10X Lysis Buffer into each well of Eppendorf twin.tec® 96 well PCR plate (VWR 47744-106), using the E4-XLS+ 8-channel pipette with multi-dispense settings of 50 µL, 4 aliquots, at aspirate and dispense speed 5.
Seal the plate and briefly centrifuge in the VWR plate spinner to collect.
This plate will cover one working week of AMP cleanups and should always be thrown away after that, or if any contamination is suspected.
Remove the 12 cDNA amplification strips from either the C1000 thermocycler or the working 4 ºC refrigerator.
PatchSeq samples will be arrayed in plastic racks holding 0.2 mL PCR tubes in two separate thermocyclers.
For PatchSeq samples, follow steps 9.2.17.1.1 – 9.2.21.
Label an Eppendorf twin.tec® 96 well PCR plate (VWR 47744-106) with the amplification name from the associated paperwork.
Together with a witness, follow the paperwork and transfer the entire contents of the PatchSeq tubes to their associated wells in the PCR plate, using an 8-channel P200 @ 60 µL.
Visually confirm the transfer of the entire volume, and transfer any remaining volume with a single channel P20, under witness, if needed.
Seal the plate and spin it down to collect the volume.
Use the Post-AMP Integra to add 0.5 µL of 10X Lysis Buffer to the strips or plate containing amplified cDNA OR add 0.5 µL manually with p2 8-channel.
This brings the final volume to 25.5 µL.
On the Coversheet, initial the box indicating 10X Lysis Buffer added to plate then encircle “0.5 µL (0.5X)” next to it.
Load the amplified cDNA in strips or a PCR plate onto the red metal Bravo 96-well block.
Orient the red block so that A1 is in upper left and H12 is in lower right.
Referencing the Coversheet, place the amplification strips according to well names: strips will have the Strip Number on A01 and Buffer Code on G01.
Strips should also carry a column ID number written on the collar of their “H” wells. Visually confirm the numbers correspond to their correct column placement.
Proceed directly to cleanup.
Bead Purification using Agilent BRAVO liquid handler
Open the "Multi-Source SPRI protocol" on V-works, located in the “Production” folder.
Bravo script for SPRI: BV-001_Multi_Source_SPRI_V2.61_(Axygen)_190314
The protocol name is found on the coversheet next to the Bravo Purification box.
From the drop-down menu, select the appropriate source plate from the container list (8 strip in Red Alum Insert).
Place the red Bravo plate containing the amplification strips on position 6 of the Bravo deck.
Referring to table found on the paperwork, enter the source volume, bead volume, and elution recovery volume.
DNA Volume = 25.60 µL
Elution Volume = 17 µL
Enter the number of columns of sample you wish to purify (use 12 for a full plate).
Make sure the "tip selection" box matches the current tip and deck loadout. Update if necessary.
Check the deck layout on V-works and ensure it matches:
After confirming the setup, remove plate seals and have a witness confirm all the selections, form entries and deck layout positions.
Initial and fill out the coversheet of the paperwork for:
Person conducting the Bravo purification.
Witness initials on “Strip Order Witness” and “Bravo Deck Witness” boxes
Circle which Bravo instrument was used.
Note the purification date.
Note the purification start time.
Run the program by clicking on the “Run MultiSource SPRI Protocol” button on the form.
Do not click on the “Run” button on the menu bar above the protocol.
Table 6 lists each BRAVO protocol step and approximate times.
Switch out tips as needed and directed (alarm will briefly sound).
Reset the tip boxes on the V-works form, the run will not continue without this.
Once directed, after the addition of Ethanol for the second wash, replace the 80% EtOH reagent trough with the Elution Buffer (EB) plate and press “continue” on the Bravo computer.
Upon completion, remove the Amplification Elution plate, seal it. Spin down at 1000 x g using POST-AMP swing-bucket plate centrifuge.
Visually confirm the presence of Elution Buffer in all the wells as the Bravo will sometimes short aspirate, or mis-aspirate completely, from one-or-more wells.
Under witness, manually recover any volume from the bead plate on a magnet to the elution plate.
Note the affected wells and lab personnel on the coversheet of the paperwork.
Some volume will remain in the bead plate as the Bravo adds 2 µL to the stated elution volume listed on the form.
Take the spun-down amplification elution plate over to the Post-AMP Integra.
Use the pre-printed plate labels to label a new Eppendorf twin.tec 96-well PCR plate (VWR 47744-106) with the associated “PG_” plate name.
Use a pre-printed FA plate label to label one of the marker plates from the 4 ºC with the associated amplification name.
Place the amplification elution plate onto the Post-AMP Integra in position “AB” on top of an Integra 96-well aluminum block.
Place the labeled PG plate onto deck position B.
Using the Post-AMP Integra, run the 3ul TWINTEK program on the Post-AMP Integra.
Follow the on-screen prompts.
Seal the PG plate and cover the amplification elution plate before ejecting the used tips into a disposable tip waste receptacle.
Load the labeled FA plate onto the Post-AMP Integra deck in position “B”.
Run the 1ul FA Plate protocol and follow the on-screen prompts.
Seal both the amplification elution plate and the FA plate.
Post-cleanup take down:
Close BRAVO software. Switch off robot and BRAVO room plate sealer.
Discard bead cleanup waste into chemical waste container.
Cap the waste container closed, but do not over tighten.
Discard used labware and wipe BRAVO deck clean.
Close the BRAVO hood and turn on UV light.
Switch off Post-AMP Integra liquid handler.
